$comment: Golden question set for Help candidate search, v1 — authored against the Evalfield School corpus (app/supabase/seeds/eval-org.sql, org eeeeeeee-eeee-4eee-8eee-eeeeeeeeeeee). Labels drafted by Claude 2026-08-15 (counter-candidate sweep + adversarial review), corrected and APPROVED by Richard 2026-08-15 — including the tuning-phase relabels; review_notes record each resolution. All people references are @eval.test emails (single identifier type). Expectation kinds: top1 (first result is who[0]); hit5 (every who ⊆ top 5); pool_only (top 5 ⊆ members holding any listed topic); pool_hit (top 5 intersects that set); empty (zero results is correct); invariants_only (asserts nothing beyond the universal invariants and must_not_surface — for pure eligibility-gate cases); stable (identical order across two runs in one transaction); order (who[] appear in this relative order among returned results). `also` nests a second expectation. acceptable_surface members are NEUTRAL: never required, never penalized — they mark labeled ambiguity; any OTHER plausible unlabeled candidate discovered later is a dataset bug (fix labels or corpus, never tune the engine to it). must_not_surface violations are HARD failures. Universal invariants checked on every case: the viewer never surfaces; members with no helper row or open_to_help=false never surface. fail_ok: true = the lexical baseline is expected to miss; excluded from pass/fail, always reported (the AI-lift ledger). layers: which test layers run the case (unit replays captured rows; integration hits the real RPC). Editing the corpus voids labels: re-run the sweep and `pnpm eval:search --capture`.

cases.question: consulting
cases.rationale: Single keyword equal to a declared topic; the rich Consulting anchor must reach the top 5. Maya (never opted in), Gus (opted out), and Otis (aspirant) are the traps.
cases.review_notes: RESOLVED (approved by Richard) 2026-08-15 (was top1, relaxed to hit5): the engine ranks Isolde Brennan ('Second-year consultant at Acme Consulting', topics Consulting+First jobs) first. On reflection that is humanly defensible — an active consultant whose title, employer, and topic all say consulting — and seniority is not something lexical search can or should fake. Isolde was already labeled acceptable. Revert to top1 [Ana] if you disagree; the engine would then need an explicit seniority/depth signal. — Approved 2026-08-15.

cases.question: venture capital
cases.rationale: All three VC helpers (rich Chloe, partial Wes, sparse Wren) in top 5, Chloe first. Traps: Capital One employer, capital-markets reporter, venture/capital split-phrase, never-a-helper VC, VC aspirant.

cases.question: medicine
cases.rationale: Rich anchor Hana and sparse Umar both in top 5. Bela (resident at a teaching hospital) is labeled acceptable — a real physician, imperfect but plausible (confirmed by Richard, 2026-08-15). Sela (biomedical PhD, Graduate school helper) is the human-obvious non-answer.
cases.review_notes: RESOLVED 2026-08-15: Richard confirmed Bela is very plausible — acceptable stands.

cases.question: looking for a consultant's perspective before I decide
cases.rationale: 'consultant' must stem-match the Consulting topic; the old substring test failed exactly this shape.

cases.question: thinking about becoming a teacher
cases.rationale: 'teacher' stems into the Teaching topic; Marco is the rich anchor. Bela's 'teaching hospital' is the stem-collision trap — a physician must not surface for a teaching-career question.

cases.question: Should I go to business school after a few years in consulting?
cases.rationale: Full sentence; the Business school anchor must survive the filler words. Ben's MBA signal lives in headline/bio/university, not his job title — realistic, and part of what the case tests. Ana (consultant) is acceptable, not required — the question's decision is the MBA. Dot (Business Manager at a School District) is the split-phrase trap.
cases.review_notes: REVIEWED 2026-08-15: kept hit5 rather than top1 — an engine ranking Ana #1 for the consulting half is humanly defensible; flip who[] to top1 to make it strict.

cases.question: How do I negotiate a job offer without losing the offer?
cases.rationale: 'negotiate' stems into the crowded 'Negotiating an offer' topic (65+ holders); the two strongest hand-authored specialists must still make top 5. Dalia's 'seasonal product offering' is the offer-collision trap.

cases.question: negotiating an offer from a startup
cases.rationale: Exactly two members hold BOTH topics (verified by sweep 2026-08-15); with 65 Negotiating-only and 20+ Startups-only competitors for 5 slots, both must make top 5 — coverage beats single-topic. Top 5 must consist of holders of one of the two topics.

cases.question: how to manage people for the first time at a startup
cases.rationale: Ember is the only Managing people + Startups holder (planted for this case). 'First jobs' holders are deliberately OUTSIDE the pool: that topic means landing your first job, not first-time management — the lexical pull of 'first time' toward them is exactly the confusion this case punishes. Traps: the People Management Group recruiter and the managing/people split-phrase member.
cases.review_notes: RESOLVED 2026-08-15: First jobs removed from the pool per review — the strict pool encodes the human reading.

cases.question: anyone from McKinsey?
cases.rationale: The three legitimate McKinsey signals — employer (Ana), employer-only (Freya), headline+history (Elias) — must all surface for a rare proper noun, regardless of their topics.

cases.question: product management in Seoul
cases.rationale: Topic plus the rare city token must beat topic-only PMs elsewhere. Zane (Production Manager — production/product stem collision) is the trap.

cases.question: INSEAD alumni advice on international MBA programs
cases.rationale: Hugo's only strong signal is the university field (C-weight); a rare proper noun there must be enough to reach top 5.

cases.question: software engineering careers
cases.rationale: The rich anchor must surface and the whole top 5 must hold the Software engineering topic — rich wrong answers (keyword-laden non-holders) are excluded structurally. Finn (paused) must be invisible despite a perfect profile.
cases.review_notes: RESOLVED (approved by Richard) 2026-08-15: Tara (sparse, topics-only) moved from must_surface to acceptable. With ~24 genuine same-topic helpers competing for 5 slots, requiring the member about whom nothing is known to make top 5 is not how a human would rank — the sparse-vs-rich principle protects sparse RIGHT answers from rich WRONG ones (now asserted via pool_only), not from richer same-topic helpers. If sparse members starving for asks matters (it does, product-wise), the fix is a rotation/exploration mechanism, not a ranking lie. Flag if you want the old label back. — Approved 2026-08-15.

cases.question: product management
cases.rationale: PM topic holders across tiers beat the stem-collision members: 'Production Manager / production lines' text matches both query stems but is the human-obvious wrong answer.
cases.review_notes: RESOLVED 2026-08-15: Ari stays acceptable. PMM is a different job than PM (positioning/GTM vs product ownership) so he is not a must — but he works alongside PMs at the same employer as the PM anchor and can genuinely speak to the role or route the asker; a possible candidate worth asking, per Richard.

cases.question: I want to talk to someone in consulting
cases.rationale: Sentence form of the consulting lookup: the anchor must surface and the top 5 must all be Consulting topic holders — the never-opted-in rich consultant, the aspirant, and the opted-out ex-consultant are excluded structurally. Note pool_only also excludes Nico (Bain consultant offering Working abroad) from the top 5, which the display cut enforces by design.
cases.review_notes: RESOLVED (approved by Richard) 2026-08-15: Sam Whitaker (sparse, topic-only) moved from must_surface to acceptable, same reasoning as sparse-software-engineering. Nico removed from acceptable because pool_only now forbids non-holders in the top 5 — his acceptability is moot under the topic-cut display rule. — Approved 2026-08-15.

cases.question: how do I get better at managing people?
cases.rationale: 77 holders compete for 5 slots: every top-5 result must actually hold the topic, and the order must be deterministic across runs. The recruiter at 'People Management Group' (employer collision) and the managing/people split member are the traps.

cases.question: interview practice and mock interviews
cases.rationale: The twins are identical except pending load (Dara has 2 seeded waiting asks, Erin 0): both must surface — their headline matches verbatim — and Erin must rank above Dara. This is the load-spreading tiebreak, observable.

cases.question: actuarial certification
cases.rationale: The viewer is the org's only actuarial helper; the correct answer to their own specialty is empty, never themself. Theo (actuarial analyst, never opted in) must also stay invisible. Question reworded from 'actuarial science exams' during QA: 'science' and 'exams' had legitimate text matches elsewhere (a science teacher, interview-prep helpers), which would have made 'empty' a wrong label.

cases.question: executive coaching
cases.rationale: Iona is the only Executive coaching helper and sits permanently at capacity (max_pending=1 with one seeded waiting ask); she would trivially rank #1 if eligible, so her absence proves the gate. Other coaches may legitimately text-match 'coaching' — the case asserts the gate, not emptiness (relabeled from 'empty' during QA).

cases.question: public speaking
cases.rationale: viewer-2 blocked Jules, the only Public speaking helper — he must be invisible to this viewer at any rank ('public' may legitimately text-match policy folks, so emptiness is not the assertion; relabeled from 'empty' during QA). Pairs with the next case, where an unblocked viewer sees him.

cases.question: public speaking
cases.rationale: Same query, unblocked viewer: Jules surfaces. Together with the previous case this proves blocking is per-pair, not global.

cases.question: restoring vintage motorcycles
cases.rationale: Nothing in the corpus relates (verified: zero token hits in the sweep). Returning anyone would mean the display floor is too permissive — empty is the correct, honest answer.

cases.question: who can help me with my first job?
cases.rationale: After stopword removal only 'first job' carries signal; a First jobs helper must reach top 5 through the filler.

cases.question: I just got laid off and I'm not sure what to do next
cases.rationale: The right helpers are Career changes people, but the question shares no stems with that phrase or their profiles. The lexical baseline is expected to miss; this is the ledger entry a future semantic stage must flip.

cases.question: I feel stuck and want a fresh start somewhere new
cases.rationale: Pure need-description with zero topic vocabulary; humans read 'career change, maybe relocation' instantly. Second ledger entry for the semantic gap.
